examples.en: I bought a compact car because it's easy to park.
Compact cars use less gas money.

examples.ko: 경차는 주차장 요금을 깎아 주는 곳이 많아요.
examples.en: Many parking lots give a discount to compact cars.
It's a compact car, so it's hard to load big luggage.

examples.ko: 저는 큰 차보다 경차가 더 좋아요.
examples.en: I like compact cars more than big cars.

examples.ko: 경차 한 대로 온 가족이 여행을 갔어요.
examples.en: The whole family went on a trip in one compact car.

explain: '경차'는 '가벼운 차'가 아니라 배기량 등 기준에 맞는 작은 차를 부르는 말이에요. '소형차'와 비슷하지만 경차가 더 작고, 세금이나 요금 혜택이 있는 경우가 많아요.

phrases.en: I drive a small compact car.
phrases.nuance_ko: 차를 운전하거나 이용한다고 할 때 '타다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: 타다 is used to say you drive or ride a car.

phrases.en: Thanks to the compact car benefit, the parking fee is cheap.
phrases.nuance_ko: 경차에 주는 세금이나 요금 할인을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the tax or fee discounts given to compact cars.

phrases.example: 가족이 늘어서 소형차에서 큰 차로 바꿨어요.
phrases.en: Our family grew, so we switched from a small car to a bigger one.
phrases.nuance_ko: 경차보다 조금 큰 작은 차예요. 비슷하지만 같지는 않아요.
phrases.nuance_en: A small car slightly larger than a 경차; similar but not the same.

explain_en: '경차' is a legal-style category for small cars (by engine size and so on), not just any light car. It is similar to '소형차' (small car), but smaller, and it often comes with tax or fee benefits.

examples.en: Adding green onion to the soup makes it taste clean and refreshing.
I bought a bunch of green onions at the market.
I slice green onions and store them in the freezer.
Green onions were expensive, so I bought only a little.
There are both onions and green onions in the fridge.

examples.ko: 대파로 만든 전을 아이들이 잘 먹어요.
examples.en: The kids eat the pancakes made with green onion well.

explain: 그냥 '파'보다 굵고 큰 파를 말해요. 국, 찌개, 볶음에 넣고 '송송 썰다', '어슷 썰다'와 같이 써요. 작은 파는 '쪽파'라고 해요.

phrases.en: One bunch of green onions costs three thousand won.
phrases.nuance_ko: 대파는 '단'으로 세어 팔 때가 많아요.
phrases.nuance_en: Large green onions are often sold counted by '단'.

phrases.en: I slice the green onion thinly and put it in the soup.
phrases.nuance_ko: 작고 둥글게 자를 때 쓰는 요리 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A cooking phrase for cutting into small round slices.

phrases.en: I trimmed the green onions before dinner.
phrases.nuance_ko: 요리하기 전에 뿌리나 시든 부분을 정리할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for trimming roots or wilted parts before cooking.

explain_en: It is a thicker, bigger kind of green onion. It goes into soups, stews, and stir-fries, and recipes say 송송 썰다 or 어슷 썰다. The small kind is called 쪽파.

examples.en: I planned the travel route in advance.

examples.ko: 이 루트로 가면 시간이 덜 걸려요.
examples.en: If you take this route, it takes less time.

examples.ko: 처음 가 본 등산 루트가 너무 어려웠어요.
examples.en: The hiking route I tried for the first time was too difficult.
The road is jammed, so let's look for another route.
Please tell me the fastest route.

examples.ko: 배송 루트가 복잡해서 하루 더 걸려요.
examples.en: The delivery route is complicated, so it takes one more day.

explain: '길'이나 '경로'보다 여행, 등산, 배송처럼 거쳐 갈 곳을 정해 둔 코스에 가까워요. '루트를 짜다', '루트를 정하다'처럼 같이 써요. 수학에서 √ 기호도 '루트'라고 읽어서 헷갈릴 수 있어요.

phrases.en: I planned the travel route with my friend.
phrases.nuance_ko: '정하다'보다 여러 곳을 어떤 순서로 갈지 계획한다는 느낌이 강해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Stronger sense of planning the order of several places than 정하다.

phrases.en: It's a good hiking route for beginners.
phrases.nuance_ko: 산을 오르는 길을 말할 때 '등산'을 앞에 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put 등산 before it to mean a route for climbing a mountain.

phrases.en: Let's decide the route first.
phrases.nuance_ko: 갈 길을 선택해서 확정한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means to choose and fix the way you will go.

explain_en: Compared with '길' (road) or '경로' (path), 'ruteu' is closer to a planned course for travel, hiking or delivery. It pairs with '루트를 짜다' and '루트를 정하다' (plan/decide a route). In math the √ sign is also read 'ruteu', so watch the context.

examples.en: I decided to enter the long jump at the sports day.
In the long jump, the run-up is very important.

examples.ko: 제 동생은 멀리뛰기를 잘해서 상도 받았어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling is good at the long jump and even won a prize.
We measured our long jump results in PE class.
A long jumper lands in the sand pit.
The long jump is easier than the high jump.

explain: 짝이 되는 종목은 '높이뛰기'예요. 학교 체력 검사에서는 제자리에서 뛰는 '제자리멀리뛰기'도 해요. 경기를 '하다', 기록을 '재다'와 자주 써요.

phrases.en: High jump and long jump are track and field events.
phrases.nuance_ko: 짝이 되는 종목인 '높이뛰기'와 함께 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used together with its paired event, '높이뛰기'.

phrases.en: We did the standing long jump in the fitness test.
phrases.nuance_ko: 달리지 않고 제자리에서 뛰는 멀리뛰기예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A long jump done from a standing position, without a run-up.

phrases.en: The teacher measured my long jump result.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뛴 거리를 잴 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A phrase for measuring how far someone jumped.

explain_en: The paired event is '높이뛰기' (high jump). In school fitness tests there is also '제자리멀리뛰기', a standing long jump. It often goes with '하다' for doing the event and '재다' for measuring the result.

examples.ko: 이 상품은 면세라서 세금이 붙지 않아요.
examples.en: This item is tax-free, so no tax is added.

examples.ko: 외국인은 면세 혜택을 받을 수 있어요.
examples.en: Foreigners can get a tax-free benefit.

examples.ko: 면세 한도를 넘으면 세금을 내야 해요.
examples.en: If you go over the tax-free limit, you must pay tax.

examples.ko: 출국할 때 면세로 사면 더 싸요.
examples.en: Buying tax-free when you leave the country is cheaper.

examples.ko: 이 가게는 면세가 안 돼서 가격이 같아요.
examples.en: This shop does not offer tax-free sales, so the price is the same.
You need a receipt to apply for tax exemption.

explain: 공항 같은 곳에서 세금 없이 파는 가게는 '면세점'이에요. 반대말은 '과세'예요. '면세'만 쓰면 상품이나 제도를 말하고, 가게 이름은 '면세점'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: I bought a present at the duty-free shop at the airport.
phrases.nuance_ko: '면세'는 제도나 상품을 말하고, 세금 없이 파는 가게는 '면세점'이라고 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: 면세 means the system or goods; the shop that sells tax-free is 면세점.

phrases.en: Duty-free goods are a bit cheaper.
phrases.nuance_ko: 세금이 붙지 않는 물건을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to goods that have no tax added.

phrases.en: This item is tax-exempt, so there is no tax.
phrases.nuance_ko: 세금을 내지 않게 된다는 뜻이에요. 물건이나 제도가 주어로 와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means it becomes tax-free; the subject is an item or system.

explain_en: A shop at an airport that sells without tax is a '면세점'. The opposite is '과세'. '면세' alone refers to goods or the system, while the shop's name is '면세점'.

examples.en: I sprinkled baking soda when cleaning.
We ran out of baking soda, so I went to the mart.

examples.ko: 이 소다는 설거지에도 쓸 수 있어요.
examples.en: This baking soda can be used for washing dishes too.
I added a spoonful of baking soda to the dough.
I scrubbed the cup with baking soda and it came out clean.
This snack has baking soda in it too.

explain: 요리와 청소에 쓰는 하얀 가루를 가리킬 때 써요. 더 정확히 말할 때는 '베이킹소다'라고 하고, 거품이 나는 물은 '소다수'라고 해요.

phrases.en: I cleaned the cup with baking soda.
phrases.nuance_ko: '소다'를 더 정확하게 부르는 이름이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the more exact name for '소다'.

phrases.en: I drank a bottle of soda water.
phrases.nuance_ko: 거품이 나는 마시는 물을 말해요. 가루 '소다'와 달라요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the fizzy drink, different from the powder '소다'.

phrases.en: The shoes smelled, so I sprinkled soda on them.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가루를 위에 뿌릴 때 '뿌리다'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Pairs with '뿌리다' when you sprinkle the powder on something.

explain_en: It refers to the white powder used in cooking and cleaning. To be more exact, say 베이킹소다, and fizzy water is called 소다수.

en: to stabilize; to settle; to equilibrate

examples.en: The medicine stabilizes the patient's condition.
The mother calmed the crying baby.
It is a policy that stabilizes prices.
I need time to calm my mind.

examples.ko: 따뜻한 차가 긴장한 몸을 안정시켜 줘요.
examples.en: Warm tea calms a tense body.
Steady your voice and try to speak.

explain: 사람이나 마음, 상태, 물가 같은 것을 흔들리지 않게 만든다는 말이에요. '안정되다'는 스스로 차분해지는 것이고 '안정시키다'는 누군가가 그렇게 만드는 거예요. '마음을 안정시키다'라고 자주 말해요.

phrases.en: Warm tea calms the mind.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common collocation.

phrases.en: The teacher calmed the angry student.
phrases.nuance_ko: 화나거나 흥분한 사람을 가라앉힐 때 특히 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Especially fits calming down someone angry or excited.

phrases.en: The government couldn't stabilize prices.
phrases.nuance_ko: 안정시키려 했지만 잘 안 됐다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means someone tried to stabilize it but could not.

explain_en: This means making a person, mood, condition or price steady. The intransitive partner '안정되다' is about becoming calm by itself, while this one is somebody making it so. 'Calm your mind' is a very common use.

examples.en: Grandfather walks slowly with a cane.
Without a cane, it is hard to walk.
I left the cane standing by the door.

examples.ko: 동화 속 마법사가 지팡이로 마법을 걸었어요.
examples.en: The wizard in the fairy tale cast a spell with his staff.
Grandmother leaned on her cane and rested for a moment.
I will give my parents a cane as a gift too.

explain: '지팡이를 짚다'처럼 '짚다'와 함께 써요. 동화나 영화에서는 마법사의 지팡이도 같은 말로 불러요. 산에서 쓰는 것은 '등산 스틱'이라고 많이 해요.

phrases.en: My leg hurts, so I use a cane.
phrases.nuance_ko: 걷는 데 도움을 받으려고 사용한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means using it to help with walking.

phrases.en: I can walk even without a cane.
phrases.nuance_ko: '없이'로 지팡이가 필요 없다는 뜻을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: 'Eopsi' says a cane isn't needed.

phrases.en: The wizard waved the magic wand.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동화나 영화에서 쓰는 지팡이예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The staff or wand seen in fairy tales and movies.

explain_en: It pairs with the verb '짚다', as in '지팡이를 짚다'. A wizard's staff in stories is also a '지팡이'. The kind used on mountain hikes is often called a '등산 스틱'.

examples.en: In games, control is important.
Your mouse control gets better with practice.
A pitcher needs good control.
I hold the Control key and copy the text.
I was not confident in my control, so I drove slowly.
Control is also hard when the car slips.

explain: '컨트롤이 좋다', '컨트롤이 안 되다'처럼 잘 다루는 정도를 말해요. 야구에서 투수가 공을 원하는 곳에 던지는 능력은 '제구력'이라고도 해요.

phrases.example: 이 선수는 공 컨트롤이 정말 좋아요.
phrases.en: This player has really good ball control.
phrases.nuance_ko: 무언가를 원하는 대로 잘 다룰 때 칭찬하는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A compliment for handling something just the way you want.

phrases.example: 너무 긴장해서 몸 컨트롤이 안 돼요.
phrases.en: I'm so nervous that I can't control my body.
phrases.nuance_ko: 마음이나 몸이 뜻대로 움직이지 않을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when your mind or body won't do what you want.

phrases.en: Controlling emotions is hard even for adults.
phrases.nuance_ko: 화나 슬픔 같은 마음을 다스리는 일을 말할 때 앞에 '감정'을 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put 감정 before it to talk about managing feelings like anger or sadness.

explain_en: 컨트롤 describes how well you handle something, as in '컨트롤이 좋다' and '컨트롤이 안 되다'. In baseball, a pitcher's ability to throw where he wants is also called '제구력'.

examples.en: Even when I am angry, I control my emotions.
The pitcher controlled the ball well.
I will manage my weight for my health.
I learned how to control the robot.
I controlled my speed and came down slowly.
The child controlled himself and did not cry.

explain: '감정을 컨트롤하다', '체중을 컨트롤하다'처럼 목적어를 앞에 두고 써요. 속도나 온도를 맞출 때는 '조절하다', 기계를 움직일 때는 '조종하다'가 자연스러운 경우가 많아요.

phrases.en: I adjust the air conditioner temperature.
phrases.nuance_ko: 속도, 온도, 양을 알맞게 맞출 때는 '컨트롤하다'보다 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: More natural than 컨트롤하다 for adjusting speed, temperature or amount.

phrases.example: 숨을 천천히 쉬면서 마음을 컨트롤해 보세요.
phrases.en: Try to control your mind by breathing slowly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대에게 한번 해 보라고 권하는 말투예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite way to suggest that the other person give it a try.

phrases.en: At first it is hard to control the ball.
phrases.nuance_ko: 잘 다루기 힘든 일을 말할 때 '-기 어렵다'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add -기 어렵다 to say something is hard to handle well.

explain_en: It takes an object, as in '감정을 컨트롤하다' and '체중을 컨트롤하다'. For adjusting speed or temperature, '조절하다' is often more natural, and for operating a machine, '조종하다'.

dis.h: loanword; control skill, emotions, or ball

p.n: 제어하다 is more formal and technical; 컨트롤하다 is casual spoken.
